SMTO-EXE-0099 — SMTO's screen request had a setting that isn't allowed

GUID: 124e6090-47ed-53aa-9666-47725a71baaa
Slug: screen-invalid-request
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: screen

What happened

  • SMTO's request to the screen tool included something that isn't allowed, such as an unknown action or an invalid position or size. It was refused before anything was captured.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask again in plain words, for example "take a screenshot of my main screen" or "read the text in the window in front". SMTO rebuilds the request from your words, which usually removes the bad setting.
  2. If the Gateway was recently updated or changed, start a New chat and ask there. A new chat uses the Gateway's current list of screen actions.
  3. If it keeps failing, open Settings › Setup › Gateways, select Check for updates, and if an Update to button with a version number appears for that Gateway, use it while no task is running there. SMTO and a Gateway on different versions can disagree about which screen settings are allowed.

What success looks like

  • SMTO returns the screenshot or text you asked for.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it, with the words you used, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste screenshots or screen contents into the report.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Screen request validation rejected the call: unknown operation, fields outside the closed schema, non-integer geometry or control characters, an option that needs a missing companion flag, or a malformed or oversized worker request.

What this means

  • Screen request validation rejected an unknown operation, invalid closed-schema fields, unsupported target/coordinate values or malformed bounded worker envelope. Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.

Why this can happen

  • Screen request validation rejected an unknown operation, invalid closed-schema fields, unsupported target/coordinate values or malformed bounded worker envelope.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the explicit target discriminator, current IDs, coordinate space and integer bounds with the advertised schema.

How to fix it

  • screen_contract.validate rejects unknown operations, extra fields, float geometry, control characters, jpeg_quality without format jpeg, ocr_max_characters without include_ocr, and geometry_version without include_screenshot; Gateway dispatch returns 405/422 for malformed ScreenRequest bodies, and the worker rejects requests over 1 MiB. Use the advertised schema, bounded integers, an explicit target type and current Gateway identities.
  • Use the advertised closed schema, bounded integers, explicit target discriminator and current selected-Gateway identities.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use the advertised closed schema, bounded integers, explicit target discriminator and current selected-Gateway identities.

How to verify the fix

  • The exact intended observation validates before native capture is dispatched.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass OS permissions, capture another Gateway, or copy screen content to diagnostics.

Technical notes

  • Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
